restoration_note: This teaching contrasts the two trees as two whole arrangements of the rational: the beautiful tree = Pillar of Glory whose five members ascend reflection→counsel→teaching(First Man, ship of waters/night)→thought(Third Ambassador, ship of fire/day)→mind(Father, in aeons of light); the bitter tree = same five faculties under self-love (reflection=law of death, counsel=exchange/furnaces, teaching=gehenna of smoke, thought=stronghold, mind=bolos). The strongest restorations come from the rigid five-faculty formula and the editor's anchored proposals (titles like ⲡⲥⲧⲩⲗⲟⲥ ⲙ̄ⲡⲉⲁⲩ, ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲛ̄ⲣⲱⲙⲉ, ⲡⲡⲣⲉⲥⲃⲉⲩⲧⲏⲥ, ⲓⲏⲥ ⲡⲡⲣⲓⲉ, doxological ϣⲁⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ ⲛ̄ⲧⲉ ⲛⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ). Heading-zone gaps in §§9-13, §§41-46, and §§55-67 remained largely unrestorable because the Coptic formulas there carry no parallels in the surviving body. The contrast 'beautiful land / bitter land' constrained the spatial summary at §§40, 69-73, and the final 'these two trees do not originate from one another' was secured by the editor's running restoration. ⲧⲟⲩⲱ-vocabulary preserved as 'convey upward' (ⲭⲉⲥⲧⲟⲩ ⲁϩⲣⲏⲓ) per stage-5 vertical-motion rule.
